name: Goethe-Zertifikat A1: Start Deutsch 1

h1.source: TB-A1 p. 27; DB-A1 §4.1; US-A1 Hören Teil 1 — short everyday dialogues between two people, one picture-supported a/b/c item per text, played twice; the example item (0) is not counted; textWords = ±15 % of the 6 sample dialogues (38–46 words)

h2.source: TB-A1 p. 27; DB-A1 §4.1; US-A1 Hören Teil 2 — public announcements (airport, station, train, shop, coach tour), the instruction understood globally, richtig/falsch, each text played ONCE; textWords = ±15 % of the 4 sample texts (34–41 words)

h3.source: TB-A1 p. 27; DB-A1 §4.1; US-A1 Hören Teil 3 — answering-machine messages, partly private, partly official (practice, company), one a/b/c item per text, played twice; textWords = ±15 % of the 5 sample texts (33–47 words)

l1.source: TB-A1 p. 32; DB-A1 §4.2; US-A1 Lesen Teil 1 — two short notes or e-mails from private or working life (messages, instructions, invitations), 5 statements richtig/falsch across both texts; textWords per text = ±15 % of 66 words (sample text 1) to 80 words (memo 01)

l2.source: TB-A1 pp. 32–34; DB-A1 §4.2; US-A1 Lesen Teil 2 — ten small ads or website snippets, two per situation: choose the one (a or b) that meets the stated need; textWords per ad = ±15 % of the sample ads (11–23 words)

l3.source: TB-A1 p. 32; DB-A1 §4.2; US-A1 Lesen Teil 3 — five very short signs or notices with their location (station, hotel, club, ticket machine), one statement each, richtig/falsch; textWords per sign = ±15 % of the sample signs (12–22 words)

s1.source: TB-A1 p. 37; DB-A1 §4.3.1; US-A1 Schreiben Teil 1 — a form (registration, booking, order) with exactly 5 gaps, filled from a short situation text about another person; 1 or 0 points per field; textWords = the situation text, ±15 % of the sample (42 words)

s2.source: TB-A1 pp. 37–38; DB-A1 §4.3.2; US-A1 Schreiben Teil 2 — a short message (note or e-mail: apology, invitation, enquiry) on 3 Leitpunkte given in the situation text, about 30 words; Anrede and Gruß are scored as the text-type criterion, never as a Leitpunkt; register is set per task (US-A1: informal to a friend; TB-A1 sample: formal to a tourist office)

sp1.source: TB-A1 pp. 44–49; DB-A1 §3, §5; US-A1 Sprechen Teil 1 — introduce yourself in several sentences from a keyword sheet (Name, Alter, Land, Wohnort, Sprachen, Beruf, Hobby; not all needed), about 80 s per candidate, then spell a word and give a number of at least two digits; 1 point each for introduction, spelling, number

sp2.source: TB-A1 pp. 44–51; DB-A1 §3, §5; US-A1 Sprechen Teil 2 — two topics (items = 2 rounds); per topic each candidate draws a word card, asks one question on the topic and answers one question from another candidate, about 60 s per candidate; 2 points per question, 1 per answer

sp3.source: TB-A1 pp. 44–52; DB-A1 §3, §5; US-A1 Sprechen Teil 3 — two picture cards with everyday objects (items = 2 rounds); per round each candidate makes one request to another candidate and reacts to one, a non-verbal reaction counts; an information question instead of a request is sent back for a new attempt; about 60 s per candidate; 2 points per request, 1 per reaction

telc.source: UT-A1 p. 5; telc exam page (not modelled by passRule)

parts.source: DB-A1 §4.1–4.2 (Hören, Lesen: 1 or 0 per item, max 15 each), §4.3 (Schreiben = Teil 1 [1 or 0 per field] + Teil 2 [mean of two raters, rounded to whole points from .5 up]), §5 (Sprechen 3 + 6 + 6, mean of two raters rounded from .5 up), §6.1 (each part × 1.66, summed, total rounded to whole points), §6.2 (Prädikate), §6.3 (≥ 60 of 100 and every part taken, no part minimum; below 35 written points 60 is out of reach), §7 (not modular; resit only as a whole)

openQuestions: Does the product need a telc view of the result for telc Deutsch A1 candidates? The same format is presented by telc as 60 raw points with 36 = ausreichend (UT-A1 p. 5); passRule holds only the Goethe rule 'goethe-a1' (DB-A1 §6: Σ raw × 1.66, rounded; ≥ 60 of 100 with every part taken, no part minimum; below 35 written points the oral cannot reach 60). A telc view would need its own rule id (e.g. 'telc-a1').

Boundary for EXM-07: 21 raw written points give 34.86 scaled (< 35) and a full oral (15 raw) gives 24.9, so the total 59.76 rounds to 60. DB-A1 §6.3 says below 35 written points taking the oral makes no sense (German) / is not allowed (English), i.e. treats it as a fail; recommend the goethe-a1 scorer treats written < 35 as not passable and pins 34.86 vs 36.52 (22 raw) in its boundary test.

Rounding: the official Schreiben Teil 2 and Sprechen results are the mean of two raters rounded to whole points (from .5 up, DB-A1 §4.3.2, §5), and the total is rounded after × 1.66 (§6.1). Our single automated score keeps half points; the goethe-a1 scorer should round S2 and the Sprechen total before scaling (E1-3 decision).

Per-Teil minutes are a design split of the official module times (Hören ca. 20 min including instructions and about 3–5 min answer transfer, Lesen 25, Schreiben 20); only the module times and about 5 min per Sprechen Teil (DB-A1 §3) are published. Re-time h1–h3 against the first generated audio.

textWords bands are ±15 % of our own word counts of one official set (US-A1, 6th ed. Feb 2024); Lesen Teil 1 text 2 is an image in that PDF and was not counted, so the l1 upper bound uses memo 01's 70–80 words. Re-count against a second official set (e.g. telc UT-A1) before the registry freeze.

Schreiben Teil 2 register is not fixed by the format (US-A1: informal e-mail to a friend, du; TB-A1 sample: formal enquiry, Sie), so the template leaves `register` open and each WritingTask sets it. Should a coverage rule require both registers across A1.1/A1.2?

Answer-sheet transfer: the paper exam gives about 5 min inside the exam time (DB-A1 §2.2; TB-A1 says about 3 min for Hören); the digital and online Goethe formats have no transfer (DB-A1 Anhang), telc A1 is paper only. answerSheetStep = true is meant for one Modelltest form only (BLUEPRINT §2.3).

Schreiben Teil 1 spelling: TB-A1 p. 37 says spelling costs points only when it harms understanding, in the paragraph after the Teil 2 rule; applying it to Teil 1 fields is our reading (numbers, dates and times stay exact).

Joint format: US-A1 (2024) says the exam was developed jointly by the Goethe-Institut and telc, while DB-A1 (Stand 1 Sept 2025) names only the Goethe-Institut as Träger; whether current telc A1 papers still match item for item was not re-checked.

transfersTo is empty on every Teil: the only other A1 lane (oza1, ÖSD ZA1) is deferred under the lean launch, and apart from the form (ZA1: 10 entries for 5 points) no ZA1 Teil has an SD1 task shape; decide when oza1 is authored.
